(c) Maintain a centralized identity access management (IAM) system, logging all access requests and approvals. 1.4. Incident Response and Regulatory Access: The Processor shall (a) Implement an incident response program, aligned with ISO/IEC 27001:2022, incorporating documented procedures for detection, containment, eradication, and recovery of Security Incidents involving KFintech/Fiduciary Personal Data. (b) Notify within twenty- four (24) hours of becoming aware of a confirmed Security Incident (as defined in General Terms), providing incident details (c) Maintain documented policies for handling regulatory or government access requests, notifying KFintech within twenty- four (24) hours of becoming aware of a confirmed Security Incident unless legally prohibited, with training for relevant personnel. 1.5. Government and Regulatory Access Requests: The Processor shall: (a) Maintain documented policies for assessing and responding to government or Regulatory Authority requests for KFintech /Fiduciary Personal Data, ensuring compliance with Applicable Law; (b) Notify KFintech within forty eight (48) hours of receiving such requests, unless legally prohibited, including request details and response provided, per Section 3.4; (c) Train personnel handling requests on regulatory requirements, with training records maintained for KFintech audits. 1.6. Supply Chain Security: The Processor shall (a) Conduct due diligence for Sub-processors and third-party vendors accessing personal data, ensuring regulatory compliance, before engagement. (b) Include data protection clauses in Sub-processor agreements, with annual compliance reviews. 1.7. Personnel Training: The Processor shall provide annual data protection and security awareness training to all personnel processing KFintech /Fiduciary Personal Data, with additional training for those handling government requests, and maintain training logs for KFintech’s review. 2. Physical Security Measures 2.1. Data Center Access Control: The Processor shall (a) Deploy on-site security guards to control and monitor access to data centers hosting personal data, operating 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, (b) Install physical access control systems (e.g., badge readers, biometric controls) at data center entry points and sensitive areas, restricting access to authorized personnel via a circle lock/mantrap to prevent tailgating. (c) Separate sensitive areas within data centers, accessible only by personnel with personal access credentials granted on a need-to-know basis, approved by management. (d) Lock technical facility rooms, maintaining on-site access control credentials with issuance registration. (e) Equip emergency exterior doors. (f) Require pre-announced, escorted access for third-party visitors and deliveries, approved by listed personnel, using secure intermediate holding areas to prevent direct access to computer systems or communication facilities. (g) Install CCTV surveillance and motion detection at key points (e.g., parking lots, reception, data center rooms), retain recordings for ninety (90) calendar days or as per legal/ regulatory requirements. (h) Monitor access via guard station personnel, with access reports and privileges audited quarterly, retaining logs for twelve (12) months. 2.2. Access Monitoring and Visitor Control: The Processor shall (a) Log all physical access events, with logs reviewed quarterly and retained for twelve (12) months. (b) Require pre-approved, escorted access for third-party visitors and deliveries, using secure holding areas to prevent direct access to sensitive areas. (c) Trigger audible alarms for unauthorized exterior door openings, with immediate security response. 2.3. Device Security: (a) Secure laptops, mobile devices, and removable media accessing Customer Data with full-disk encryption (e.g., BitLocker). (b) Maintain an inventory of devices accessing Customer Data, with annual audits to ensure compliance. 2.2. Continuous Monitoring: The Processor shall review and update physical security measures semi-annually to address infrastructure changes or emerging threats, with updates documented for KFintech’s audits. 2.3. Secure Disposal: The Processor shall use secure methods (e.g., shredding, degaussing) for disposing of physical media containing KFintech /Fiduciary Personal Data, maintaining disposal logs for KFintech review. 3. Technical Security Measures 3.1. System and Network Security: The Processor shall (a) Implement a kind of architecture or equivalent requiring continuous verification for system and network access, with micro-segmentation to isolate personal data environments. (b) Deploy firewalls, intrusion prevention systems (IPS), and endpoint detection and response (EDR) solutions, and 24/7 monitoring. (c) Harden hosts and virtual servers by disabling unnecessary services, applying security patches 3.2. Access Controls: The Processor shall (a) Enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) using biometrics or hardware tokens for systems processing personal data, with unique user IDs. (b) Log all access events, with automated alerts for suspicious activity reviewed within twenty-four (24) hours, retaining logs for twelve (12) months. (c) Disable inactive accounts after specific timeframe as per KFintech policies and enforce password policies requiring 10-character minimum, complexity (uppercase, lowercase, numeric, special), and periodic rotation. 3.3. Encryption: The Processor shall (a) Encrypt personal data in transit using SSL/TLS 1.2 and above, with quantum-resistant algorithms where supported. (b) Encrypt personal data at rest (c) Ensure Sub-processors or third parties do not access encryption keys without KFintech’s approval, with key rotation every twelve (12) months. 3.4. Vulnerability and Threat Management: The Processor shall (a) Conduct yearly penetration tests and vulnerability scans on systems and applications, remediating critical vulnerabilities within seven (7) days. (b) Deploy anti-malware and EDR solutions with real-time scanning, automatic updates, and monthly full-system scans, integrated with a SIEM system. 3.5. Network Isolation and Data Transmission: The Processor shall (a) Segregate production networks from corporate and public networks using VLANs, private IP connections, and strict access control lists (ACLs). (b) Protect end-user sessions with HTTPS and secure API gateways, ensuring no unencrypted data transmission. 3.6. Software Security: The Processor shall (a) Implement a secure SDLC for applications processing personal data, including static/dynamic application security testing (SAST/DAST) and code reviews. (b) Require Information Security Group approval for software installations, with annual audits. 3.7. Monitoring and Logging: The Processor shall (a) Enable security event logging on to all systems and applications, analyzed via SIEM, with logs retained for twelve (12) months. (b) Monitor production systems 24/7, with automated alerts for anomalies actioned within twenty-four (24) hours. 4. Data Management Measures 4.1. Data Access and Input Control: The Processor shall (a) Restrict personal data access to authorized personnel via RBAC, logging all read, write, or delete actions. (b) Verify input, edit, or deletion through ITIL-based change control processes, with quarterly reviews. 4.2. Data Separation: The Processor shall (a) Logically segregate personal data by KFintech using partitioning, with access via MFA security gates. (b) Prohibit transfer to corporate environments unless approved, with annual audits. 4.3. Data Retention and Deletion: The Processor shall (a) Retain personal data only as required by Annex [X] or Applicable Law, deleting within ninety (90) calendar days of Agreement termination or KFintech’s request. (b) Securely delete data from disks, backups, and archives using cryptographic erasure, providing written certification to KFintech. (c) Maintain legally required backups in encrypted, restricted form, deleted upon expiry. 4.4. Backup and Recovery: The Processor shall (a) Maintain encrypted (AES-256) backups in geographically diverse locations, tested annually for recovery. (b) Ensure service restoration within four (4) hours of disruption, with redundant power, cooling, and networking. 4.5. Security Incident Management: The Processor shall (a) Implement an incident response program, aligned with ISO/IEC 27001:2022, incorporating documented procedures for detection, containment, eradication, and recovery of Security Incidents involving KFintech /Fiduciary Personal Data. (b) Notify KFintech within twenty- four (24) hours of becoming aware of a Security Incident, providing impact and remediation details. (c) Support KFintech investigations with logs and reports, retaining incident records for twelve (12) months. 4.6. Compliance Verification: The Processor shall (a) Maintain valid ISO27001 certification with annual audits covering personal data processing activities and provide audit certificates and reports to KFintech upon request. (b) Support KFintech’s audits per Processor Terms, providing ISMS documentation and third-party controls.
